item.title: Hiroshima Okonomiyaki Cooking Class: Build Your Own — Guide
item.description: Hiroshima okonomiyaki looks simple and is deceptively hard: the layering, the timing and above all the flip of a tall, loose stack take real skill, which is exactly what makes a cooking class here so satisfying. In a small group around a teppan griddle, an instructor walks you through spreading the thin crepe, piling on the cabbage and pork, steaming it down, frying the noodles alongside and finally combining and flipping the whole thing without collapse, before finishing with sauce, seaweed and bonito flakes.

item.title: Hiroshima-style Okonomiyaki: Layered, Not Mixed — Guide
item.description: Okonomiyaki is Hiroshima’s proudest food, and locals will tell you firmly that theirs is the original and superior version. Unlike the Osaka style, where everything is mixed into a batter, Hiroshima okonomiyaki is built in layers: a thin crepe is spread on the griddle, then piled high with shredded cabbage, bean sprouts and pork belly, pressed down as it steams, and finally set on a nest of fried soba or udon noodles and topped with a fried egg and a slick of sweet-savoury sauce.

item.title: Osaka Okonomiyaki Guide: The Savoury Pancake, Done the Osaka Way
item.description: Okonomiyaki — literally “grill what you like” — is the hearty, savoury griddle pancake that, with takoyaki and kushikatsu, completes Osaka’s holy trinity of konamon (flour foods). A batter of flour, egg, and mountains of shredded cabbage is mixed with your choice of pork, seafood, or cheese, griddled on a hot teppan, then lacquered with sweet-savoury okonomiyaki sauce, mayonnaise, seaweed, and bonito flakes. Filling, cheap, customisable, and deeply satisfying, it’s Osaka home cooking turned restaurant ritual.
